All four lenses — ux, bugs, onboarding, content — score Mode A journey evidence, and lenses read a run folder rather than driving the browser themselves. Traversal count scales with *modes × personas × sites*, not with lens count:
- A second persona would add a second traversal.
- A `technical` objective would add a Mode B measurement pass, and `seo`/`aeo` a Mode C crawl — different capture shapes, not re-drives of this one.

reply:
**2 captures.**

| Capture | Mode | Feeds |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Mode A-visit** (persona-driven visit — `traversal-visit`) | clarity, conversion, trust |
| 2 | **Mode C** (session-less crawl — `traversal-crawl`) | seo |

The arithmetic: your four objectives collapse into two capture modes, not four. Clarity, conversion and trust are all scored off the *same* A-visit evidence — one persona walking the site with a question, producing screenshots, session log, timeline and debrief. Three lenses read that one body of evidence afterwards. SEO can't reuse it, because it needs a no-persona, no-session crawl recording per-page markup facts (titles, meta, canonicals, headings, structured data, internal links, robots, sitemap) — different driver, different output shape.

So: 2 captures, 4 scoring passes.

One dependency worth naming up front, since it's the only thing that changes the number: **captures scale per persona, lenses don't.** If the interview lands on one persona, it stays at 2. Two personas means two A-visit captures (4 lenses… still 1 crawl), so 3 captures total. The Mode C crawl is always exactly 1 regardless — it has no persona to vary.

Also note conversion specifically requires a stated conversion goal in the target file. Without one that lens has nothing to measure against, but it doesn't add a capture — it's a prerequisite on capture 1, not a third capture.

**Default run folder:** outside your repo — `~/.understudy/runs/<product>-<timestamp>/`. A run writes a lot of evidence (screenshots per step, session log, timeline, raw observations, debrief, then the lens reports), and none of it is your product's source. **What I do about git:** nothing, without asking.

The reason the default sits outside the repo: capture artifacts from a logged-in persona routinely contain material you don't want pushed — session cookies and tokens in the network log, real account data in screenshots, sometimes internal URLs. Keeping them out of the tree by default means an accidental `git add -A` can't publish them.

That's what CLAUDE.md §7 exists to prevent: no real product names, URLs, credentials or run traces in the plugin, by construction rather than by discipline.

Where it can go instead:

- **`~/.understudy/runs/<slug>/`** — the default. Outside any repo, nothing to gitignore.
- **`<your product's repo>/understudy-runs/<slug>/`** — explicitly allowed; it's your product and your call. The interview offers to add it to *that* repo's `.gitignore`, and init refuses until it's ignored.
- **Any other folder you name**, as long as it's not inside the plugin.

If what you're actually after is versioned artifacts, the third option with a repo you control gets you there — the plugin repo can't, at any setting.
